Title: Active/Associate Membership
Headline: Active/Associate Membership
MetaDescription: Practicing Urologists Within AUA Section Boundaries Mid-Year Savings Special!
Body:
Practicing Urologists Within AUA Section Boundaries

Mid-Year Savings Special!
Save 50% on Your AUA Dues for 2026!

United States and Canada: $625 $313

Mexico and Central America: $369/$333/$295* $185/$167/$148*

The prestige of belonging to the AUA is embedded in its long history as an established, trusted and transparent organization. As an Active or Associate member of the AUA, you can be assured that wherever you are in your career, the AUA has tools and opportunities to help you succeed.

Explore Benefits for Active and Associate Members!

  • Enjoy major savings on the AUA Annual Meeting, featuring the latest science and education in the field of urology.
  • Access discounted and member-only resources for continuing medical education (CME) and lifelong learning from the AUAUniversity.
  • Enjoy complimentary online access to AUA’s family of publications, including The Journal of Urology®, Urology Practice®, AUANews and JU Open Plus. ☨
  • Stay at the forefront of patient care with the AUA clinical practice guidelines.
  • Let your voice be heard as the AUA advocateson the federal, state and local levels of government to promote and preserve the interests of the specialty.
  • Continue growing your career with the Institute of Leadership and Business, featuring the AUA Leadership Program, exchange programs, educational resources and more.
  • Get involved with advancing the AUA’s mission by volunteering to serve on an AUA committee.
  • Receive up-to-date clinical resources for your practice and free patient education materials on urologic conditions through our official foundation, the Urology Care Foundation.

Join Today

Active and Associate Membership Eligibility and Requirements

Eligible applicants for Active Membership must be a practicing urologist in the United States, Canada, Mexico or Central America who is:

  • in possession of an unlimited license to practice medicine and surgery in the state, province or country where they practice
  • in possession of a Medical Doctor (MD) or Doctor of Osteopathic Medicine (DO) degree (or United States Medical Licensure equivalent) and has completed a urology residency program accredited by ACGME (or equivalent accreditation organization) or the certifying board for urology in the country where practicing.
  • practicing solely in the specialty of urology.
  • certified by the American Board of Urology (ABU), American Osteopathic Board of Surgery (AOBS), or the certifying board for urology in the country where practicing.

A copy of your medical license and proof of board certification is required as part of the application. The AUA will reach out to the ABU to verify board certification. Individuals certified by another board entity will need to provide documentation directly to the AUA.

Associate Membership

  • Eligibility requirements for Associate membership are the same as Active membership, except for Board certification.

Note: Active and Associate members must also be members of their AUA Section. Upon completion of the AUA membership application, the application will be forwarded to the applicant’s Section of residence for processing. The Section will then reach out to the applicant for a separate Section dues payment (if applicable).

*Dues for Active/Associate members in countries outside the U.S. and Canada (within AUA Section boundaries) are stratified according to the World Bank classification of country. View membership dues by country.

☨Print subscriptions to The Journal of Urology® and/or Urology Practice® can be purchased by members for an additional fee. Learn More

Senior Membership: Active or International members with 20 or more years of membership who are retired or permanently disabled may apply for Senior Membership (dues exempt). Please call a Member Services representative at 410-689-3933 to check your membership record before applying.

Group Billing: The AUA offers group billing to urology residency programs and medical practices. For more information, or to enroll, please contact the Member Services department at 410-689-3933 or membership@auanet.org. Coming Soon: Online enrollment and payment.

Dues Reduction Request: In special circumstances, AUA members may qualify for reduced or waived dues on an annual basis. The AUA offers these options to help members maintain their membership in good standing through unexpected or difficult conditions. Active, Associate, International and Associate-in-Transition members are eligible to apply for reduced dues ($190) should a full dues payment be considered a financial hardship for the reasons listed on the application. An AUA member may request a waiver of dues if payment would be considered a financial hardship by reason of temporary physical disability or illness. Once submitted, the Member Services department will review the application and notify you of the approval status.

Title: International
Headline: International
MetaDescription: Practicing Urologists Outside of AUA Section Boundaries Mid-Year Savings Special!
Body:
Practicing Urologists Outside of AUA Section Boundaries

Mid-Year Savings Special!
Save 50% on Your AUA Dues for 2026!

2026 Membership Dues: $369/$333/$295* $185/$167/$148*

For more than a century, the AUA has stood at the forefront of developing innovative, evidence-based quality education for urologists and urology health care professionals worldwide. We are committed to providing our members with urologic education to enhance patient care around the world through the collaboration and exchange of knowledge and resources.

Explore benefits for International Members!

  • Enjoy major savings on the AUA Annual Meeting, featuring the latest science and education in the field of urology.
  • Access discounted and member-only resources for continuing medical education (CME) and lifelong learning, including multi-language webinars, from the AUAUniversityandAUAUniversity Spanish.
  • Stay at the forefront of patient care with the AUA clinical practice guidelines, including a selection oftranslated guidelinesproduced in collaboration with international society partners.
  • Enjoy complimentary online access to AUA’s family of publications, including The Journal of Urology®, Urology Practice®, AUANews and JU Open Plus.
  • Assist your patients with a broad selection of translated patient education resources from the Urology Care Foundation.

Join Today

International Membership Eligibility and Requirements

Eligible applicants for International Membership must be:

  • a urologist (Doctor of Medicine degree or equivalent) actively practicing outside the United States, Canada, Mexico or Central America
  • a member of their national urological society

A $50 application fee is required as part of the application.

*dues for International members are stratified according to the World Bank classification of country. View membership dues by country.

To access membership dues rates for those residing in countries outside the United States within AUA Section boundaries, including Canada and Mexico, click here.

Group Billing: The AUA offers group billing to urology residency programs and medical practices. For more information, or to enroll, please contact the Member Services department at 410-689-3933 or membership@auanet.org. Coming Soon: Online enrollment and payment.

Dues Reduction Request: In special circumstances, AUA members may qualify for reduced or waived dues on an annual basis. The AUA offers these options to help members maintain their membership in good standing through unexpected or difficult conditions. Active, Associate, International and Associate-in-Transition members are eligible to apply for reduced dues ($190) should a full dues payment be considered a financial hardship for the reasons listed on the application. An AUA member may request a waiver of dues if payment would be considered a financial hardship by reason of temporary physical disability or illness. Once submitted, the Member Services department will review the application and notify you of the approval status.

Title: Research Scientist Membership
Headline: Research Scientist Membership
MetaDescription: Research Scientists, Doctors of Veterinary Medicine, and Non-Practicing MDs Mid-Year Savings Special!
Body:
Research Scientists, Doctors of Veterinary Medicine, and Non-Practicing MDs

Mid-Year Savings Special!
Save 50% on Your AUA Dues for 2026!

2026 Membership Dues: $221 $111

The AUA provides support to urology researchers of all backgrounds, including MDs and PhDs engaged in basic, translational and clinical research across the spectrum of urologic diseases. Whether you are conducting research or want to stay up-to-date on the latest breakthroughs, membership in the AUA provides the tools and resources to support your professional mission.

Explore Benefits for Research Scientist Members!

  • Research Scientist members are eligible for funding awardsprovided through both the AUA and the Urology Care Foundation, which has provided nearly $30 million to advance the careers of over 750 investigators since 1975.
  • Take advantage of a variety of grant writing and fundingopportunity workshops, dynamic research conferences and other resources.
  • Take part in the AUA Urology Scientific Mentoring and Research Training (USMART)Academy, which carries the mission of fostering creative and impactful mentorships between developing urology physician-scientists and established investigators.
  • Enjoy major savings on the AUA Annual Meeting, featuring the latest science and education in the field of urology.
  • Enjoy complimentary online access to AUA’s family of publications, including Urology Practice®, AUANews and JU Open Plus. You may also accessThe Journal of Urology®online for only $100 per year!Explore Subscription Options
  • Stay at the forefront of patient care with the AUA clinical practice guidelines.

Join Today

Research Scientist Membership Eligibility and Requirements

Eligible applicants for Research Scientist Membership must be:

  • an independent investigator with a PhD or equivalent degree or
  • a Doctor of Veterinary Medicine or
  • a non-practicing MD and/or related professional

who has demonstrated achievements in the field of urology through research or has made substantial contributions to urologic research in an administrative capacity.

A copy of your Curriculum Vitae (typed or printed clearly in English) and a $50 application fee is required as part of the application.

  • Receive up-to-date clinical resources for your practice and free patient education materials on urologic conditions through our official foundation, the Urology Care Foundation.

Join Today

Allied Membership Eligibility and Requirements

Eligible applicants for Allied Membership must be:

  • primary urology healthcare team members, including:
    • nurses (LPN, LVN, RN)
    • technicians
    • medical assistants

As part of the membership application, nurse applicants are required to submit a current nursing license. Technicians are required to submit a letter written by a practicing urologist on letterhead confirming they have completed in-service training in the field of urology under their supervisor. Medical assistants are required to submit written evidence of current CMA certification.

A $50 application fee is also required.

Body:
More Information about the American Urological Association

Board of Directors

The Officers and Section Representatives of the Board of Directors (BOD) of the AUA serve as the governing board of American Urological Association, Inc., and American Urological Association Education and Research, Inc. Urology Care Foundation, Inc. is the officiation foundation of the AUA and is managed by a separate board comprised of urologists and public (non-urologist) members.

The 13 voting members of the BOD include the President, President-elect, Immediate Past President, Secretary, Treasurer and one elected representative from each of the AUA's eight chartered Sections. If the regularly-elected Section representative to the Board of Directors is absent, their place is filled by the elected alternate, or by a designee of the Section. The Historian, Secretary-elect and Treasurer-elect are non-voting members.

View a complete list of the AUA's current Board of Directors.

Education to Meet Your Needs

For more than a century, the AUA has stood at the forefront in developing innovative, evidence-based quality education for urologists and urologic health professionals worldwide - throughout all stages of their careers. Explore all the opportunities available to AUA members at a free or discounted rate!

  • Meetings/Courses:
    • Calendar of Events– Whether you are looking for a course, seminar or meeting, visit this page to view the most current list of both domestic and international events.
    • Annual Meeting– The AUA's Annual Meeting offers you the latest science and exciting interaction with your colleagues, as well as subject-oriented and surgical-learning courses.
    • Section Meetings– Visit each Section's website to find information on their regional Annual Meeting.
  • Products/Programs:
    • Urology Core Curriculum– AUA's Core Curriculum is the most comprehensive reference guide available detailing the knowledge necessary to deliver quality urological care; and is FREE for members! The reference guide links to the most up-to-date and scientific resources available.
    • Educational Products– AUAUniversity offers year-round access to a growing repository of valuable information through live and online educational opportunities, apps, webcasts, books, publications and much more.
    • Guidelines– AUA's Clinical Practice Guidelines provide evidence-based guidance with an explicit clinical scope and purpose. You can also download the AUA Guidelines-at-a-Glance mobile app on the App Store or Google Play Market.
  • Publications:
    • The Journal of Urology® is the most widely read and highly cited journal in the field, providing the clinically relevant content needed to stay at the forefront of the dynamic field of urology. The Journal of Urology® is published monthly and mailed to more than 18,000 subscribers.
    • Urology Practice® focuses on clinical trends, challenges and practical applications in the areas of business, health policy, the specialty and patient care.
    • AUANewsis the official news magazine of the AUA. It is published monthly online.
    • NetNews is a bi-monthly e-newsletter from the AUA featuring important updates for members.
    • The AUA Daily Scope is a daily digest of urology news and scientific updates emailed to you every morning.

Dues payments must be submitted to the AUA by December 31 for the upcoming year. Dues received after the deadline are assessed a 10 percent late fee.

For your convenience, the AUA offers several payment options:

  • Online: The easiest and fastest way to renew is online at my.AUAnet.org. Log in using your email and password to pay by Visa, MasterCard, Discover and American Express. Since payments are registered automatically, benefits will go uninterrupted as soon as payment is received.
  • Phone: Credit card payments can be processed over the phone by contacting AUA Member & Customer Services at 410-689-3700.
  • Mail: Mail a copy of your invoice with payment information to the address below. If sending in a check, please make it payable to the American Urological Association, include your AUA ID#, and mail it to:

    American Urological Association, Inc.


    P.O. Box 791002
    Baltimore, MD 21279-1002

NOTE: Please do not send questions/correspondence with your invoice and payment. If you use the return envelope with your invoice, your payment will be mailed to the P.O. Box used by our bank. While correspondence mailed to the P.O. Box address reaches our office, it may take several weeks for it to arrive. Therefore, it is important to mail your correspondence, especially time-sensitive requests, to our office address: AUA Member & Customer Services, 1000 Corporate Blvd., Linthicum, MD, 21090, USA. You may also call us at 410-689-3700, or email CustomerService@AUAnet.org for further questions and concerns.

The AUA offers these options to help members maintain their membership in good standing through unexpected or difficult conditions. Review the requirements for a dues reduction or exemption to see if you qualify.

In addition, Active or International members with 20 or more years of consecutive AUA membership who are fully retired from practice or permanently disabled may apply for Senior Membership (dues exempt). Please call 410-689-3700 to check your membership record before applying.

Resident/Fellow members who have graduated from residency are transferred to Fast-Track Associate Membership (unless we are notified that they are currently in a fellowship). Fast-Track Associate members' dues are discounted for up to two years. Once passed the two-year mark, dues are no longer discounted and members pay the same rate as Active and Associate Members.

No, in order to register for the Annual Meeting as a member, you must first renew your membership.

Title: Journal Peer Reviewers
Headline: Journal Peer Reviewers
MetaDescription: The AUA has three official peer-reviewed journals: The Journal of Urology® is the most widely read and highly cited publication in the field providing...
Body:
The AUA has three official peer-reviewed journals:

The Journal of Urology® is the most widely read and highly cited publication in the field providing physicians with all the clinically relevant information necessary to stay at the forefront of the dynamic specialty of urology.

Urology Practice® focuses on clinical trends, challenges and practice applications in the four areas of Business, Health Policy, the Specialty and Patient Care.

JU Open Plus is an international, peer-reviewed, open access publication providing authors with continuous publication of high-quality research in all areas of urology. Article types accepted for submission include full-length original research articles, narrative and systematic reviews, letters to the editor, editorials, video articles, research communications, commentaries, and case reports/case series.

The Editors are always looking for volunteers to build-up our current reviewer database.
Job Requirements: Area of expertise needed varies based on article topic.
Time Commitment: Review time is based on article topics published monthly and is based on area of expertise.
AUA Contact:Daniel T. Kulp

Body:
The Content Review Workgroup reports to the AUA Education Council and oversees all AUA-sponsored CME activities to ensure educational materials are scientifically valid and free of bias. Activities include educational courses throughout the year, sessions at the Annual Meeting, affiliated sub-specialty and society meetings, section meetings of the AUA, printed educational materials as well as eLearning programs. The content review process is entirely web-based and consists of peer reviewers who are expert physicians covering all major areas of sub-specialization in urology.
Job Requirements: Practicing physicians 1-5 years out of residency and beyond fellowship training.
Time Commitment: Individuals typically conduct reviews 1-10 times per year (throughout the year).

Title: The FUTURE Urologist Mentorship Network
Headline: The FUTURE Urologist Mentorship Network
MetaDescription: The FUTURE Urologist Mentorship Network, powered by Qooper, connects medical students with mentorship opportunities, resources, and a community to help them prepare for a career in urology.
MetaKeywords: FUTURE Urologist Mentorship Network, FUTURE Urologist
Body:
The FUTURE Urologist Mentorship Network, powered by Qooper, connects medical students with mentorship opportunities, resources, and a community to help them prepare for a career in urology.

The AUA’s FUTURE in Urology Program is proud to offer the FUTURE Urologist Mentorship Network. The AUA’s FUTURE in Urology Program is a comprehensive incubator program designed to support the pipeline, mentorship, and promotion of pre-medical, medical students, and urology trainees. The FUTURE Urologist Mentorship Network is a private, online community that allows mentees (medical students interested in pursuing urology as a specialty) to connect with volunteer mentors to support their journey to, and through, urology.

Frequestly Asked Questions

  • Who is eligible to be a mentee?

The FUTURE Urologist Mentorship Network was conceived to help grow the number of medical students in the urology pipeline by creating meaningful mentorship opportunities. The platform is open to all medical students and residents who are seeking mentors in urology.

  • Who is eligible to be a FUTURE Mentor?

Any AUA member urologist (board-certified or board-eligible) at fellow or attending level (i.e. independent clinical practice) and independent researchers.

  • How do I use the FUTURE Urologist Mentorship Network platform?

Simply create a free account and build your profile. Then you can connect with others, message mentors or other mentees, and access training and resources.

  • Does it cost anything to be part of the platform?

No, access to the platform is free.

  • Do I have to be an AUA member to use the platform?

While AUA membership is not required, we encourage everyone in the urology community to be an AUA member. AUA membership is free for medical students. Learn More

  • Who do I contact if I have questions?

For technical issues, please contact info@qooper.io. For questions about the AUA FUTURE in Urology Program, please contact kmaab@auanet.org.

Title: International
Headline: International
MetaDescription: AUA is Proud to be the Most Global Organization in Urology!
Body:
AUA is Proud to be the Most Global Organization in Urology!

The AUA is a global membership organization and is proud that roughly 25% of its membership resides outside the United States. To better meet the needs of members around the world, AUA provides significant discounts on annual dues for international members — urologists save up to 52% off AUA’s domestic dues rate! The AUA is mindful of the economic disparities around the globe; international membership dues are stratified based on the World Bank Classification of Countries.

The AUA is committed to advancing urology around the world, and we invite the global urologic community to become members of the AUA and enjoy the many benefits of membership, like subscriptions to The Journal of Urology® and AUA’s family of publications, major savings on Annual Meeting, access to the Urology Core Curriculum and other exclusive content in AUAUniversity and more.

Here are ways the AUA serves the global urologic community:

Through LEADERSHIP

The AUA has dedicated leadership for each region of the world who are focused on establishing strong and mutually beneficial collaborations with our partners around the world.

David F. Penson, MD, MPH, MMHC
AUA Secretary

Jorge Gutierrez-Aceves, MD
Associate Secretary, Americas & Caribbean

Jose A. Karam, MD, FACS
Associate Secretary, Europe, Middle East & Africa

Jaspreet S. Sandhu, MD
Associate Secretary, Asia & Australia

Through GLOBAL PARTNERSHIPS

The AUA has an International Member Committee (IMC), comprised of representatives from international urological societies around the world that have at least 75 members in the AUA International and International-Resident-in-Training categories. The international societies that comprise the IMC are AUA’s priority partners and are provided special opportunities to engage with, and contribute to, AUA’s array of programming and activities, including:

  • Input and engagement with AUA leadership
  • Invitations to provide speakers, moderators and abstract reviewers
  • Invitations to participate on AUA editorial boards
  • Opportunities to contribute to AUANews
  • Opportunities to contribute to AUA’s Global Connections e-newsletter
  • Opportunities to participate in exclusive programs like the AUA Residents Bowl competition at Annual Meeting

Through EDUCATION

The AUA has a dedicated International Programs team that produces more than 60 custom educational activities around the world each year. In 2022 and 2023, these activities spanned six continents, and included the first ever AUA Annual Review Course in Kuwait. For more information about international educational partnerships, please email Lori Agbonkhese, Director of International Programs.

AUA Annual Meeting

The AUA Annual Meeting is the largest, most global event in urology and welcomes thousands of international attendees from around the world. The 2024 Annual Meeting included attendees from more than 100 countries outside of the United States! The AUA is proud that its annual meeting serves as a beacon for the global urologic community. International society programs are a key feature of the Annual Meeting each year, as well as the AUA’s popular International Prostate Cancer and International Bladder Cancer Forums. These programs underscore the value global perspectives bring to the AUA meeting.

Members save! AUA members save up to $886 on Annual Meeting registration, so it pays to be an AUA member! The 2025 meeting will take place in the dynamic city of Las Vegas, NV. Become a member, and join us in Las Vegas!

Translated Guidelines

Through valuable partnerships with international societies, the AUA has translated a selection of clinical guidelines.

Explore Today

Multi-language Webinars

With support from educational grants from our industry partners, the AUA has produced several free webinar series in multiple languages, including Spanish, Portuguese and Mandarin.

View Now

AUAUniversity en Español

AUAUniversity is the largest online repository of urologic education in the world. A wide selection of education is available in Spanish and can be found on the AUAUniversity Spanish site.

View Today

Through EXCHANGES & SCHOLARSHIPS

The AUA's Academic Exchange and Visiting Scholar Programs provide young urologists the opportunity to gain a global perspective in urology while broadening their cultural horizons. The AUA offers

2024 Exchange Scholars enjoy time together during the AUA Presidents Reception at the Grand Hyatt San Antonio River Walk.

Learn More

through HUMANITARIAN EFFORTS

The Urology Care Foundation, the official foundation of the AUA, is committed to supporting humanitarian health care missions in urology. The Foundation has launched a series of humanitarian endowments to support missions that will improve the urologic health in underserved areas across the globe. Learn more about

Dr. Stephanie Kielb, a recipient of a UCF humanitarian grant, leads a healthcare mission in Rwanda.

Explore Today

Through PATIENT EDUCATION

The Foundation's Website, UrologyHealth.org, is dedicated to providing the most trusted, up-to-date information on urologic conditions and includes hundreds of free resources for patients and their caregivers. Thanks to our valuable partnerships, most of these materials have been translated into Spanish, and selected materials have been translated into Arabic, Brazilian Portuguese, French, Gujarati, Hindi, Italian, Punjabi, Urdu and Vietnamese. We invite you to explore these resources and share with your patients.

Title: Medical Student Membership Workgroup
Headline: Medical Student Membership Workgroup
MetaDescription: Since launching its Medical Student membership category in 2012, the AUA has seen extensive growth in this unique membership segment and now boasts more...
Body:
Since launching its Medical Student membership category in 2012, the AUA has seen extensive growth in this unique membership segment and now boasts more than 2,000 medical student members worldwide. In Fall 2023, the AUA Section Secretaries Membership Council (SSMC), approved the formation of a Medical Student Membership Workgroup to help the AUA better understand and meet the needs of medical students looking to pursue a career in urology.

The membership of the Medical Student Membership Workgroup includes eight voting medical student members, representing the geographic boundaries of the eight AUA Sections, as well as representatives from the Latino Medical Student Association, R. Frank Jones Urological Society, The Society of Women in Urology and Urology Unbound. In addition, the Committee includes physician liaisons from the AUA Health Advancement & Impact Committee, AUA Medical Student Education Committee, AUA Residents and Fellows Committee and the Society for Academic Urologists.

Workgroup Mission:

The Medical Student Membership Workgroup will foster and grow a strong network of engaged medical students that can facilitate AUA’s understanding of medical student needs. It will also aim to expand AUA’s reach and influence among medical students while supporting efforts to engage medical students from all demographic backgrounds in the field of urology.

Key Initiatives of the Medical Student Membership Workgroup include:

  • Medical Student Mingle – Hosted immediately after the Medical Student Forum at the AUA Annual Meeting, this popular event provides both organic and structured networking opportunities for medical students.
  • Medical Student Speed Mentoring — This program connects medical students with current urology residents and fellows to support them on their journey toward becoming urologists.
  • SAU/AUA Urology Match Insider podcast series– Developed by the Society of Academic Urologists in partnership with the AUA, these interviews give medical students an inside look at the Urology Residency Match process.

Title: Advanced Practice Provider Committee
Headline: Advanced Practice Provider Committee
MetaDescription: Taylor Brewer, PA-C, MS, BS APP Committee Team Lead, Advanced Practice Providers (APPs) are a vital force in urology, playing a key role in delivering...
Body:
Taylor Brewer, PA-C, MS, BS

APP Committee Team Lead,

Advanced Practice Providers (APPs) are a vital force in urology, playing a key role in delivering exceptional, patient-centered care. With over 1,800 members and growing rapidly, APPs now represent the fastest expanding membership segment within the AUA.

To support this momentum, the AUA’s APP Committee brings together 12–15 passionate Advanced Practice Providers—balanced between Physician Assistants (PAs) and Advanced Practice Nurses (APNs)—alongside two urologists committed to advancing education for non-physician providers. Reporting to the AUA Education Council, the committee is strategically organized into three focused subcommittees: Member Engagement, Live Education, and Online Education.

The Member Engagement Subcommittee, which also connects with the Section Secretaries Membership Council, leads efforts to grow and engage the APP community. Their mission: to ensure that AUA membership delivers real value by aligning programs, resources and benefits with the evolving needs of APPs in urology.

Recent activities and initiatives of the Member Engagement Subcommittee include:

  • APP of the Year Award– an annual award designed to recognize the outstanding contributions of APPs working in urology.
  • Why Urology?– hear from APPs working in urology as they share what they love about the specialty!
  • Advancing Your Career: Strategies & Best Practices for APPs Working in Urology- hear from Advanced Practice Providers (APPs) working throughout the career timeline of an APP. Gain insights into advancing your career at every stage with advice and personal experiences from your peers.
  • Navigating the Urology Team: The APP - Physician Dynamic- In the fast-paced world of urology, collaboration is key to delivering optimal patient care. Navigating the Urology Team: The APP-Physician Dynamic podcast episode explores the crucial partnership between Advanced Practice Providers (APPs) and Physicians.

If you’re not a member, join us! To connect with the APP committee, email us at appmembership@auanet.org.

Title: AUA Advanced Practice Provider of the Year Award
Headline: AUA Advanced Practice Provider of the Year Award
MetaDescription: The AUA Advanced Practice Provider (APP) of the Year Award was established by the 2019-2020 AUA APP Membership Committee led by Chair, Tricia Zubert, APRN, CNP, to recognize the contributions and accomplishments of APPs in the field of urology. Since that time, the APP Membership Committee selects a recipient to be honored with the award each year.
Body:
The AUA Advanced Practice Provider (APP) of the Year Award was established by the 2019-2020 AUA APP Committee led by Chair, Tricia Zubert, APRN, CNP. This prestigious award celebrates the remarkable achievements and invaluable contributions of APPs in urology. Each year, the APP Committee proudly selects a deserving recipient to receive this honor, highlighting the exceptional impact these professionals have in the field.

Natalie Barganski, DNP, APRN, CPNP-PC, RNFA

2026 Award Winner

Natalie Barganski is a nationally recognized leader in pediatric urology whose clinical expertise, educational leadership, and dedication to advancing the Advanced Practice Provider (APP) role make her an exceptional candidate for the APP of the Year Award. Since joining Driscoll Children’s Hospital in 2009, she has elevated pediatric urologic care through her expertise in urodynamics, management of complex bladder disorders, and commitment to evidence-based, patient-centered care. As a Pediatric Urodynamic Trainer, Past Chair of the PUNS Urodynamic Special Interest Group, and Co-Founder and Instructor of the Pediatric Urodynamic Course, she has trained and mentored APPs and nurses nationwide, helping expand the scope and impact of APP-led specialty care. Through her clinical excellence, national education efforts, and community advocacy for children with complex urologic conditions, Barganski continues to advance the field while serving as a role model for current and future APPs.

2027 APP of the Year nominations will open in November 2026.

Eligibility

Recipients must meet the following criteria to be eligible:

  • Demonstrates strong leadership skills in urology while advancing the APP role and enhancing APP visibility both regionally and nationally.
  • Delivers outstanding patient care by driving change through the implementation of evidence-based practices and innovative practice models.
  • Significantly contributes to the APP program at their respective Section/Society meeting and/or shows leadership in coordinating other APP activities/initiatives
  • An AUA Advanced Practice Provider (APP) Member in good standing who does not currently serve on the AUA APP Committee.

Winners receive a $1,000 stipend to attend the AUA Annual Meeting. The winner will be presented with their award during the APP Program (Urologic Care for the Advanced Practice Provider).

Questions? Contact Jordan Malloy at appmembership@AUAnet.org.

Body:
The AUA’s International Member Committee (IMC) is comprised of representatives from international urological societies around the world that have at least 75 members in the AUA International and International-Resident-in-Training categories. The international societies that comprise the IMC are AUA’s priority partners and are provided special opportunities to engage with, and contribute to, AUA’s array of programming and activities. Representing the international voice of the AUA, the IMC provides thought leadership, feedback and counsel to the AUA Board of Directors on the needs and challenges faced by the international urologic community. In addition, the Committee works to expand the AUA’s member offerings globally and to enhance engagement between urologic professionals all over the world.

Body:
Matthew Lee, MD, MBA

The Residents and Fellows Committee (RFC) represents the voice of resident/trainee members for the AUA. As a member of the AUA Section Secretaries/Membership Council, the committee aims to advance the concerns and needs of medical students, residents and fellows to the AUA, its regional Sections, and its affiliate organizations and partners abroad.

The membership of the Residents and Fellows Committee includes representatives from each of the eight AUA Sections and from Canada and Mexico, as well as liaisons from the American Medical Association, the American College of Surgeons and the Residency Review Committee for Urology of the Accreditation Council for Graduate Medical Education.

The RFC organizes several activities and events each year to engage and connect residents and trainees. Highlights include:

  • The AUA Residents Forum– The largest gathering of residents and fellows at the Annual Meeting, the Residents Forum explores the topics most relevant to residents and fellows.
  • AUA Residents and Fellows Committee Teaching Award– The RFC coordinates this annual award to highlight extraordinary educators in urology.
  • AUA Residents and Fellows Committee Essay Contest– This annual competition gives medical students, residents and fellows the opportunity to share their experience and insights on a particular theme through the power of the written word.
  • Residents Bowlat the Annual Meeting – The RFC brings spirited competition to each Annual Meeting through this popular event.

Body:
The AUA Residents and Fellows Committee Teaching Award annually recognizes an outstanding urology educator or program director who has dedicated a portion of their career to teaching residents.

2026 Teaching Award Winner

Melissa R. Kaufman, MD, PhD, FACS

Patricia and Rodes Hart Professor of Urologic Surgery
Chief of Division of Reconstructive Urology and Pelvic Health
Vanderbilt University Medical Center

Dr. Melissa R. Kaufman is Professor, Patricia and Rodes Hart Endowed Chair of Urologic Surgery, and Chief of the Division of Reconstructive Urology and Pelvic Health at Vanderbilt Medical Center. Her practice focuses on female and male voiding dysfunction and incontinence, cancer survivorship, pelvic organ prolapse, neurourology, transitional care for congenital urologic conditions, urologic prosthetics, transgender surgery, as well as reconstructive surgery for urethral stricture, fistula, and trauma. Dr. Kaufman was recently honored with a Distinguished Mid-Career Award by the American Urological Association and the F. Brantley Scott Innovation Award for her contributions in urologic prosthetics. Her most impactful awards have been endowed by her trainees, including the Department of Urology Resident Teaching Award and the Vanderbilt Section of Surgical Sciences McCleery Master Teacher Award.

“Dr. Kaufman’s dedication to teaching, her innovative methods of feedback, and her unwavering commitment to excellence make her the ideal candidate for this award. We are endlessly grateful for her time and attention and know that our future patients will be as well.”

-Kate Dwyer, MD, JD; Will Furuyama, MD; Lan Anh Galloway, MD; and Bryn Lautner, MD
Vanderbilt University Medical Center

“She models excellence at all times across the spectrum of her exceedingly busy and complex clinical practice. She exhibits patience and honesty in each encounter with her patients, colleagues, and trainees. Despite ever-present clinical and research demands, she remains patient, honest, and thoughtful. Our trainees universally feel supported by her, personally and professionally.”

-Kristen R. Scarpato, MD
Associate Professor of Urology, Residency Program Director, Vice-Chair of Education Department of Urology
Vanderbilt University Medical Center

Eligibility

Eligible nominees must meet the following requirements:

  • Participation as a program director of and/or faculty member in an accredited urology residency program within AUA Section boundaries.
  • Evidence of dedication and effectiveness in teaching residents.
  • Behaviors which are value-based and highly principled.
  • An exemplary role model.

The winner will be presented with their award during the Residents Forum program at the 2026 Annual Meeting in Washington, DC.

The Teaching Award nomination cycle is now closed. Please check back in Fall 2026 for the 2027 submissions guidelines.

Body:
Jyoti D. Chouhan, DO, PharmD, MBA, FACS

Young Urologists Committee Chair

As part of the AUA Section Secretaries/Membership Council, the Young Urologists Committee represents the voice of early-career urologist members of the AUA. A "young" urologist is defined as a urologist (who has completed training) who has been in practice for ten years or less.

The membership of the Young Urologists Committee includes the Chair, Next Chair, Immediate Past Chair, representatives from each of the eight AUA Sections as well as one Doctor of Osteopathy representative and one active duty military representative. In addition, the Committee also includes liaisons from the Residents and Fellows Committee, Advanced Practice Provider Committee, American College of Surgeons (ACS), American Medical Association Young Physicians Section and AUA Leadership Program.

Activities and initiatives of the Committee include:

The Young Urologists Forum — A perennial favorite at Annual Meeting, the YU Forum explores topics impacting today’s young urologists.

Speed Mentoring for Residents — Held annually at the Annual Meeting, this event was created to foster a greater connection with residents and support them in their career growth and development.

Young Urologist of the Year Awards — This esteemed awards program recognizes young urologists who are making an impact in the specialty.

Transitioning from Residency to Practice Manual — The YU Committee updates this manual annually with advice and information on transitioning to practice.

To connect with the YU Committee, please email us at youngurologists@AUAnet.org.

Title: Journal Subscriptions

Body:
New for 2026: We’re Evolving to Better Serve You – Digitally!

As the world of publishing continues to shift away from print, we’re adapting to meet the needs of our members where they are – online, on-demand and on the go! Beginning in January 2026, we will transition to online-only journal subscriptions for members. This change reflects a broader industry trend and will allow us to provide a more environmentally friendly solution while delivering content faster and more flexibly. The online versions will be continuously updated as original investigations, comprehensive reviews and commentary become available, providing up-to-the-minute access to the latest science impacting the specialty. Plus, the journals will be adding more dynamic content, including videos and podcasts, providing even greater insights for our members. If you still wish to receive a printed version of The Journal of Urology®, or Urology Practice® you will be able to purchase the print edition by selecting the option below.

The Journal of Urology®

The Journal of Urology®, the official journal of the AUA and the most widely read and highly cited journal in the field, provides extensive coverage on the clinically relevant content needed to stay at the forefront of the dynamic field of urology. This premier journal presents investigative studies on critical areas of research and practice, survey articles with short condensations of the best and most important urology literature worldwide and practice-oriented reports on significant clinical observations.

Online Subscription – $100

Print & Online Subscription – $500

Urology Practice®

Urology Practice®, an official, peer-reviewed journal of the AUA and companion to The Journal of Urology®, focuses on clinical trends, challenges and practical applications in the areas of business, health policy, the specialty and patient care. Coverage includes clinical practice articles, original studies, articles on the business of urology, content for urology care team members and more.

Print & Online Subscription – $250

Purchase Print + Online Subscription

Subscriptions are only available to members. If you are not a member of the AUA, we encourage you to join to receive access to our journals.

Benefits of Your Digital Subscription

Instant access to the latest research. No need to wait for a monthly delivery—the journals are continuously updated as original investigations, comprehensive reviews and commentary become available. Authors benefit, too, as novel research can be shared more widely and more quickly, generating greater awareness of your work.

Earn free CME! Get the most of your Journal of Urology® subscription with the FREE JU Home Study. Access monthly clinically relevant articles and complete the online post-test to earn up to 12 AMA PRA Category 1 Credits™ throughout the year.

Access over a century of content anytime, anywhere! Tap into more than 100 years of rich and storied history and content on your phone, tablet, or laptop—wherever you need it. The intuitive search of The Journal makes it easy to pinpoint the information you need.

Still want the print edition? If you still wish to receive a print subscription to The Journal of Urology® or Urology Practice®, the annual subscription prices are $500 and $250, respectively, per year.

New for 2026: Online-only Subscriptions to The Journal of Urology®

If you are a current member who does not receive a JU subscription as a benefit of membership, you may now purchase an online-only subscription for $100 per year.

Title: Frequently Asked Questions Changes to Your Journal Subscriptions
Headline: Frequently Asked Questions
MetaDescription: Frequently Asked Questions Changes to Your Journal Subscriptions
MetaKeywords: Frequently Asked Questions Changes to Your Journal Subscriptions
Body:
Changes to Your Journal Subscriptions

Why are you eliminating the printed versions of JU and UPJ?

The publishing industry has undergone major changes over the past several years as the world consumes content in more digital ways, and digital publishing has become the industry standard.

The true value of the journals is in their content, and you will continue to enjoy anytime access to this content online. This transition will also allow the AUA to enhance its digital editions with more multimedia content like videos and podcasts, providing our members with even greater insights into the studies and science shaping our specialty.

What if I still want a print edition of the journals?

As a member, if you still wish to receive a print subscription to The Journal of Urology® or Urology Practice®, you can purchase an annual print subscription of JU for $500 per year and UPJ for $250 per year. Subscriptions are only available to members. If you are not a member of the AUA, we encourage you to join to receive access to our journals.

I already receive the online version of the journal and have opted to purchase a print subscription. Why has the cost increased for my print subscription?

Unfortunately, the price for printing the journal has increased substantially – from supplies to production to postage. The previous subscription cost no longer covers these expenses and the AUA can no longer subsidize these costs.

I’m having trouble accessing the digital version, how do I access it?

You will need your AUA ID and login to access.

If you are still having trouble, email AUA Customer Service, or reach them by phone at 1-410-689-3700.

How will I be notified when a new issue comes out?

You will receive a monthly email announcing the issue release. Please remember to check your spam folders to ensure you are receiving this email.

Manage your JU and UPJ communication preferences anytime.

Access to the Journal is not included in my membership. Do I still have the option to purchase access?

If you are a current member who does not receive a subscription to The Journal of Urology®, or Urology Practice® you have the following subscription purchase options:

  • The Journal of Urology® print+online: $500 per year

Title: Creating visual abstracts to promote your research: A how-to guide
Headline: Creating visual abstracts to promote your research: A how-to guide
MetaDescription: Social media (e.g. Twitter, Facebook, Instagram) are platforms heavily used by medical professionals, and the lay public, to communicate and share results from research studies. Visual abstracts, which are visual representations of research articles, are visually engaging and concise ways of sharing the results of studies on social media. The use of visual abstracts to promote research, as measured by impressions on Twitter, has been shown to dramatically increase the numbers of individuals who review and learn about the research.
Body:
Denzel Zhu1, Alex Sankin, MD1,2

  • Albert Einstein College of Medicine, Bronx, NY
  • Department of Urology, Montefiore Medical Center, Bronx, NY

Contact information: denzel.zhu@einsteinmed.org, asankin@montefiore.org

Social media (e.g. Twitter, Facebook, Instagram) are platforms heavily used by medical professionals, and the lay public, to communicate and share results from research studies. Visual abstracts, which are visual representations of research articles, are visually engaging and concise ways of sharing the results of studies on social media. The use of visual abstracts to promote research, as measured by impressions on Twitter, has been shown to dramatically increase the numbers of individuals who review and learn about the research. 1,2 However, there are few guidelines on creating effective visual abstracts. Our goal here is to provide guidance on creating an effective visual abstract, based on our past experience. 3

Abstract Design

We used Microsoft PowerPoint v16.64 (Microsoft, Redmond, WA)’s default slide size of 16:9 (Widescreen) to create our abstract. In general, we divide the slide into three major sections: the header (where the journal logo and visual abstract title go), the body of the abstract (where the study’s methodology, exposure, and outcomes are listed), and the footer (where the study’s conclusion, citation, and abstract author’s byline and contact information are listed, as well as institutional logos from the author’s institution; Figure 1).

Figure 1. Structure of the visual abstract.

For the title of the abstract, we recommend against replicating the study title for the visual abstract. Rather, we suggest writing the central question that the study is attempting to answer. For example, our recent study’s title was “Finasteride and risk of bladder cancer in a multiethnic population”. However, the central question our study was attempting to answer was: “Did the chemoprotective effect of finasteride for the prevention of bladder cancer vary by race/ethnicity?” The question provides more context for viewers of the visual abstract, and creates a narrative tension that the remainder of the visual abstract can provide the answer to.

For the body of the abstract, we suggest using the methodology space to describe overall characteristics of the study population, such as the number of participants, their demographics, and the inclusion criteria. For the exposure and outcome spaces, we suggest filling these spaces with the exposure of the study (e.g. drug vs placebo) and the relevant outcome of the study (e.g. the risk of developing bladder cancer). In the footer of the abstract, we suggest placing the major conclusion of the study, along with information for viewers to find more information about the study and the author’s institution and contact information (i.e., Twitter handle).

Style Choices

We suggest using large, bolded, easily readable fonts to write out information within the visual abstract. Given that many abstracts will be viewed on mobile devices, or compressed when uploaded to social media networks, there will be limits on how much text which can be included in the abstract. In the abstract below, we used size 22 font, Arial for headers, and size 18 font, Arial for the main text.

We also suggest using icons, many of which are freely available for noncommercial purposes, to emphasize certain points within the abstract. There are many icons which describe clinical elements, and are available from icon repositories such as Noun Project and Flaticon. However, we caution authors that certain icons are licensed as “Creative Commons” and require attribution to the icon creator. However, many icons are licensed as either public domain (which do not require any attribution at all) or rights to use icons can be purchased for a nominal fee (generally <$10.00).

Lastly, we recommend using complementary color palettes when designing your abstract. Complementary color palettes improve readability and the visual appeal of your abstract. Many are freely available at Coolors.co. These color palettes can then be used to create backgrounds for specific information you wish to highlight in your abstract.

Reviewing

Once we incorporated all design elements, we developed the abstract below (Figure 2). However, we emphasize the need for multiple individuals to review and provide feedback on the abstract. Additionally, before posting the abstract to social media websites, we recommend exporting the abstract from Microsoft PowerPoint as a PNG file and reviewing it, to ensure that design elements remain consistent in the export process.

Figure 2. Finalized abstract.

Conclusions

Visual abstracts are an effective way of promoting research findings on social media, and for concisely communicating key findings to other researchers and the lay public. Within this blog post, we have provided some guidance on the creation of visual abstracts. We hope other members of the urologic community utilize this novel method of research outreach and communication.

Further Reading

NephJC Website—NephJC is a nephrology Twitter journal club that creates many high quality visual abstracts based on the nephrology literature. Their website contains many great examples of visual abstracts, and can be viewed for inspiration.

Andrew M. Ibrahim, MD, Creative Director at Annals of Surgery, provides an excellent guide on creating a visual abstract.

References

  • Lindquist LA, Ramirez-Zohfeld V. Visual Abstracts to Disseminate Geriatrics Research Through Social Media. J Am Geriatric Soc. 2019;67(6):1128-1131.
  • Ibrahim AM, Lillemoe KD, Klingensmith ME, Dimick JB. Visual Abstracts to Disseminate Research on Social Media: A Prospective, Case-control Crossover Study. Ann Surg. 2017;266(6):e46-e48.
  • Zhu D, Srivastava A, Agalliu I, et al. Finasteride Use and Risk of Bladder Cancer in a Multiethnic Population. J Urol. in-press, doi:10.1097/JU.0000000000001694.

Body:
Submit an Article

The APC for JU Open Plus full-length articles is $2,800 (USD) for non-members and discounted to $2,400 (USD) for AUA members for the Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-NoDerivatives 4.0 International Public License, as currently displayed at http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc-nd/4.0/legalcode (the “CC BY-NC-ND") and $1,000 (USD) for non-members and discounted to $850 (USD) for AUA members for case reports, case series, research reports, and commentaries published under the CC BY-NC-ND license.

JU Open Plus offers full or partial equitable waivers for accepted articles from low- and middle-income economies. Eligibility is based on the Research4Life eligibility criteria. Countries listed in Group A are eligible for the full waiver, and countries listed in Group B are eligible for the partial (50%) waiver. The waiver is automatically applied based on the Corresponding Author’s country information provided during submission. To determine your eligibility, visit the Research4Life criteria page at https://www.research4life.org/access/criteria/.

Please be advised that JU Open Plus will only refund an APC if an editorial error has resulted in a failure to publish an article under the OA terms selected by the authors. APCs will not be refunded when articles are withdrawn voluntarily due to author error or misconduct.

OA articles are freely available to read, download, and share from the time of publication under the terms of the Creative Commons License Attribution-Non-Commercial-No Derivative (CC BY-NC-ND) license. This license does not permit reuse for any commercial purposes, and it does not cover the reuse or modification of individual elements of the work (such as figures, tables, etc.) in the creation of derivative works without specific permission.

Authors retain their copyright for all OA articles. Authors grant American Urological Association Education and Research, Inc. an exclusive License to Publish the article, and the article is made available under the terms of a Creative Commons user license.

Body:
The AUA's Academic Exchange Programs provide junior faculty and residents an opportunity to interact with and learn from colleagues in different regions of the world. These funded fellowship programs encourage the interchange of urological skills, expertise and knowledge, which are critical to the continued success of urology worldwide. In addition to a unique educational and cultural experience, academic exchange programs offer scholars the opportunity to interface directly with the leadership of the AUA and other international urological associations, which can lead to professional opportunities in the future. As technology continues to advance at a rapid pace, the exchange of knowledge will continue to increase resulting in a higher quality of care to our patients. However, Academic Exchanges provide face-to-face interaction and the ability to network, which remain critically important to the advancement of urology.

Title: International Exchange Programs
Headline: International Exchange Programs
MetaDescription: The AUA’s Academic Exchange Programs provide promising young urologists the opportunity to gain a global perspective in urology while broadening their cultural horizons.
MetaKeywords: Exchange Programs, Brazil, China, Europe, India, Japan, Urologic Education, International Programs
Body:
The AUA's Academic Exchange Programs provide promising young urologists the opportunity to gain a global perspective in urology while broadening their cultural horizons. These reciprocal programs include a 2-4 week educational experience at an academic institution(s) and attendance at the national society's annual meeting. During the exchange, participants observe urologic surgeries/procedures, attend clinics, present lectures and take part in staff activities. The exchanges are "observation only" – participants do not perform hands-on surgery.

The AUA offers academic two-way exchange programs with the following countries/regions:

Exchange participants are selected through a competitive application process (application deadlines and eligibility requirements vary by program). Interested faculty must submit an online application and supporting documentation. Each application is then reviewed by the appropriate selection committee. Applicants are scored and ranked on a number of criteria that includes, but may not be limited to, the following:

  • Commitment to academic urology, including fellowships and/or scholarships during residency or post-residency
  • Research productivity (clinical or laboratory), including grants received, commitment to laboratory investigation, current research in progress and current research program
  • Achievements in and commitment to clinical urology
  • Record of publications, peer reviewed and other
  • Commitment and contributions to the AUA (at national and/or Section level) – papers presented, program chairmanships, postgraduate or other courses taught and committee service
  • Strength and relevance of candidate's personal statement
  • Strength and enthusiasm of letter of support from program chair

The program not only allows the sharing of knowledge and experiences, but is designed to foster a closer alliance between the AUA and SBU and assists in identifying future leaders within both organizations.

This reciprocal program includes a 2-3 week educational experience at an academic center(s) in Brazil with attendance at an SBU urology meeting. During the exchange, the participant observes urologic surgeries/procedures, attends clinics, presents lectures and takes part in staff activities. Program Schedule

Scholars will spend 2-3 weeks visiting Brazilian host institution(s) and will attend the SBU Sao Paulo Congress on September 2-6, 2026.

MetaKeywords: Europe, European Urology Association, EAU, International Exchange Programs, Urology Education
Body:
In 1993, the AUA and the EAU began an award program designed to provide young urology faculty with an international perspective on urologic medicine. The program not only allows for the sharing of knowledge and experience but is designed to foster a closer alliance between the AUA and EAU, and assists in identifying future leaders within both organizations. During the odd numbered years, European urologists visit centers in North America, and in even numbered years, North American urologists travel to European host sites.

This reciprocal program includes a 2-week educational experience at academic centers in Europe and attendance at the EAU Annual Meeting. During the exchange, participants observe urologic surgeries/procedures, attend clinics, present lectures and take part in staff activities. The exchanges are "observation only" – participants do not perform hands-on surgery.

Program Requirements

European scholars will spend up to two weeks visiting European institutions and will attend the Annual Meeting of the European Association of Urology on March 13-16, 2026 in London, United Kingdom.

Eligibility Requirements

To be eligible for the program, the candidate must be:

  • 45 years of age or younger (at time of application)
  • have a Medical Doctor (MD) or Doctor of Osteopathic Medicine (DO) degree, have completed all of their residency and/or fellowship training and be board eligible or certified
  • full-time academic appointment of assistant professor or higher
  • a member of the AUA
  • available to travel for up to three (3) weeks in March 2026

Title: Chakrobortty Fellowship Program
Headline: Chakrobortty Fellowship Program
MetaDescription: The AUA/Indian American Urological Association (IAUA) Chakrobortty Fellowship Program in partnership with the Puli Pradip Reddy Memorial Fund at Cincinnati Children's Hospital. Funded in part by the AUA, IAUA, and Puli Pradip Reddy Memorial Fund at Cincinnati Children's Hospital, this program promotes the interchange of urological skills, expertise and knowledge.
MetaKeywords: Academic Exchanges, Fellowships, Indian American Urological Association, IAUA, International Programs, Urology Education, Chakrobortty Fellowship
Body:
The AUA, in collaboration with the Indian American Urological Association, provides outstanding and promising junior faculty members in India with an opportunity to interact with colleagues in North America.

Medical advances are often the result of collaboration and this program has the potential to directly impact the educational opportunities for young urologists while improving the delivery of quality care to patients in India. This level of collaboration also allows for the sharing of knowledge and experience, but also enhances the global perspectives while fostering a closer alliance between the AUA and USI.

Program Details

This program allows two Indian scholars to visit U.S. host institutions for a 2-3 week period and attend the AUA Annual Meeting being held in Washington, DC on May 15-18, 2026. The selected scholars will observe urologic surgeries/procedures, attend clinics and staff activities, but will not perform surgery or hands-on patient care. The scholars will be provided a stipend to support his/her stay.

Selected scholars agree to begin working on securing their visas promptly. Additionally, selected scholars must be able to present English-translated, up-to-date immunization records. Commonly required immunizations by U.S. hospitals include, but are not limited to:

  • Hepatitis B
  • Measles, mumps, and rubella (MMR)
  • Tetanus, diphtheria, and acellular pertussis (Tdap)
  • Varicella
  • Influenza
  • FDA-approved COVID-19 vaccines, and
  • Tuberculosis (TB)

Two selected scholars may be in any urology subspecialty area; however, an interest in BPH is encouraged and host institutions will be determined at a later date.

Eligibility Requirements

To be eligible for the program, the candidate must be:

  • a urologist in India and be a member of the local or national urological organization in India
  • 42 years old or younger (at time of application)
  • MD or MBBS degree and rank of instructor or higher
  • a certified practicing urologist (within first 10 years of practice)
  • a member of the AUA
  • able to demonstrate competent command of the English language
  • able to proactively assist in obtaining visa (as needed) and communicate consistently via email with AUA staff
  • able to travel for up to 2-3 weeks

Application Process

The candidate must fill out an online application and submit electronic versions of the following documents:

  • Curriculum Vitae (CV)
  • Personal statement (300 words or less) describing how participation in the program will benefit him/her both personally and professionally
  • A letter of support from department chair (must be signed and on letterhead)

Application Deadline

Applications for the 2026 program have now closed. For additional information, please contact International@auanet.org.

Interested faculty must submit an online application and supporting documentation. Each application is then reviewed by the appropriate selection committee. Applicants are scored and ranked on a number of criteria that include, but may not be limited to, the following:

  • Commitment to academic urology, including fellowships and/or scholarships during residency or post-residency
  • Research productivity (clinical or laboratory), including grants received, commitment to laboratory investigation, current research in progress and current research program
  • Achievements in and commitment to clinical urology
  • Record of publications – peer-reviewed and other
  • Commitment and contributions to the AUA (national and/or Section) – papers presented, program chairmanship, postgraduate or other courses taught and committee service
  • Strength and relevance of candidate's personal statement
  • Strength and enthusiasm of letter of support from program chair

Body:
The AUA/CAU Visiting Scholar program allows one urologist within the regions of CAU’s membership to visit the United States, during which the scholar observes urologic surgeries/procedures, and attends clinics and staff activities. The scholar does not perform surgery or hands-on patient care. The program fosters the alliance between the AUA and Confederación Americana de Urología (CAU) and assists in identifying future leaders within those organizations.

Program Details

This program allows one CAU scholar to visit a U.S. host institution for a 2-3 week period and attend the AUA Annual Meeting being held in Washington, DC on May 15-18, 2026.

Selected scholars agree to begin working on securing their visas promptly. Additionally, selected scholars must be able to present English-translated, up-to-date immunization records. Commonly required immunizations by U.S. hospitals include, but are not limited to:

  • Hepatitis B
  • Measles, mumps, and rubella (MMR)
  • Tetanus, diphtheria, and acellular pertussis (Tdap)
  • Varicella
  • Influenza
  • FDA approved COVID-19 vaccines, and
  • Tuberculosis (TB)

Eligibility Requirements

To be eligible for the program, the candidate must be:

  • a practicing urologist within the regions of CAU's membership
  • a certified practicing urologist (within first 10 years of practice)
  • 42 years of age or younger (at time of application)
  • a member of the local or national urological organization in his/her country
  • a member of AUA and CAU
  • able to demonstrate competent command of the English language
  • able to proactively assist in obtaining a visa (as needed) and communicate consistently via email with AUA staff
  • able to travel to the United States for up to 2-3 weeks

Application Process

The candidate must fill out an online application and submit electronic versions of the following documents:

  • Curriculum Vitae (CV)
  • Personal statement (300 words or less) describing how participation in the program will benefit him/her both personally and professionally
  • A letter of support from department chair (must be signed and on letterhead)

Application Deadline

Applications for the 2026 program have now closed. For additional information, please contact International@auanet.org.

This collaborative and exciting program fosters the alliance between the AUA and the AFU.

Funding is provided for two scholars to visit North American host institutions for up to 2 weeks and then attend the AUA Annual Meeting being held in Washington, DC on May 15-18, 2026. The selected scholars will observe urologic surgeries/procedures, attend clinics and staff activities, but will not perform surgery or hands-on patient care.

Selected scholars agree to begin working on securing their visas promptly. Additionally, selected scholars must be able to present English-translated, up-to-date immunization records. Commonly required immunizations by U.S. hospitals include, but are not limited to:

  • Hepatitis B

  • have an interest in Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia (BPH) treatment

Title: International Urology Resident Programs
Headline: International Urology Resident Programs
MetaDescription: The AUA's International Resident Program allows residents from Brazil, Japan, India and China to attend the AUA Annual Meeting. The program is intended to provide potential first-time visitors to the United States and/or to the Annual Meeting with a comprehensive meeting experience and exposure to cutting-edge science on a broad range of urologic topics.
MetaKeywords: Resident Programs,Brazil, Japan, India and China, AUA Annual Meeting, Urology Residents
Body:
The AUA's International Resident Program allows residents from Brazil, Japan, India and China to attend the AUA Annual Meeting. The program is intended to provide potential first-time visitors to the United States and/or to the Annual Meeting with a comprehensive meeting experience and exposure to cutting-edge science on a broad range of urologic topics. The residents will also take part in AUA social events where they will interact with members and leaders of the Association.

Each year, residents are identified by their respective national urological associations, and each scholar's curriculum vitae is provided to the AUA. The AUA then develops a comprehensive educational track for each scholar to take full advantage of the AUA Annual Meeting; mentors are also chosen by the AUA to ensure a successful experience for each resident.

Round-trip airfare is provided by each resident's national urological association. The AUA provides complimentary hotel accommodations, meeting registration and tickets to AUA events.

The AUA International Resident Scholar Program is a unique and important opportunity for interested residents from these four countries. For more information or to learn how to apply, contact international@auanet.org.

The AUA collaborated with Astellas and Pfizer Oncology to assess current practice patterns related to utilization combination therapy as first-line treatment for metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer (mHSPC). The AUA collaborated with Pfizer Oncology to assess current practice patterns pertaining to germline and somatic HRRm testing for prostate cancer and to identify existing practices to improve patient care. The AUA collaborated with Johnson & Johnson to assess current practice patterns around the use of miscellaneous J codes in urologic practice settings. Title: Optimizing First-Line Management of Metastatic Hormone-Sensitive Prostate Cancer
Headline: Optimizing First-Line Management of Metastatic Hormone-Sensitive Prostate Cancer
MetaDescription: The Advanced Prostate Cancer guidelines from the American Urological Association (AUA) and Society for Urologic Oncology provide a strong recommendation...
Body:
The Advanced Prostate Cancer guidelines from the American Urological Association (AUA) and Society for Urologic Oncology provide a strong recommendation that patients with mHSPC should be treated with ADT in combination with an APRI or docetaxel. Although combination therapy improves survival of mHSPC patients and is recommended by national guidelines, evidence indicates that many patients do not receive this treatment approach.

Recognizing the importance of implementing first-line combination therapy in the treatment of mHSPC, the AUA, in collaboration with Astellas and Pfizer Oncology, conducted focus groups and interviews with healthcare providers in a variety of practice settings to understand current practice patterns and identify barriers and best practices to improve utilization of combination therapy for mHSPC.

This resource provides insights into best practices for those seeking to improve the treatment of patients with mHSPC.

Title: Integrating Biomarker and Genetic Testing for HRR Mutations into Prostate Cancer Management
Headline: Integrating Biomarker and Genetic Testing for HRR Mutations into Prostate Cancer Management
MetaDescription: Testing for homologous recombination repair mutations (HRRm) for prostate cancer patients can provide insights that may guide targeted treatment...
Body:
Testing for homologous recombination repair mutations (HRRm) for prostate cancer patients can provide insights that may guide targeted treatment decisions, inform prognosis and provide familial risk implications for family members.

Recognizing the value of genetic and biomarker testing in the management of prostate cancer, the American Urological Association (AUA) collaborated with Pfizer Oncology to assess current practice patterns pertaining to germline and somatic HRRm testing for prostate cancer and to identify existing practices to improve patient care. This was accomplished by developing and fielding a survey to AUA members in the United States to assess current practices and challenges related to germline and somatic HRRm testing for prostate cancer, and developing an infographic to display key results of the survey. Additionally, AUA staff conducted in-depth qualitative interviews with representatives from three practices who manage prostate cancer patients. From these interviews, several key findings emerged for practices for integrating HRRm testing into the management of prostate cancer patients.

While there is no one-size-fits-all model for every program, this resource offers valuable insights for those looking to efficiently and effectively integrate biomarker and genetic testing to provide personalized care for prostate cancer patients.

Title: Practical Strategies for the Use of Miscellaneous J Codes in Urology Practice
Headline: Practical Strategies for the Use of Miscellaneous J Codes in Urology
MetaDescription: Practical Strategies for the Use of Miscellaneous J Codes in Urology Practice
MetaKeywords: Practical Strategies for the Use of Miscellaneous J Codes in Urology Practice
Body:
Urology practices need confidence that they will be appropriately reimbursed when providing patient access to newly FDA-approved drugs and therapies during the period before a permanent J code is established. However, billing with miscellaneous J codes can be complex and administratively burdensome, often creating uncertainty about whether full reimbursement will be received. This lack of confidence can delay adoption of new treatments and, ultimately, patient access to clinically appropriate therapies.

Recognizing the importance of timely patient access to newly FDA-approved drugs and therapies, the AUA, in collaboration with Johnson & Johnson, conducted focus groups, a membership survey, and interviews with healthcare professionals across a variety of practice settings. The objective was to assess current practice patterns related to the use of miscellaneous J codes, identify barriers to their effective implementation, and uncover best practices that could support more efficient integration and utilization of miscellaneous J codes within urology practices.

This practice resource provides practical, actionable insights into current barriers to use of miscellaneous J codes, operational strategies to manage or overcome these barriers, and identifies best practices for efficient integration into operational workflows.

Body:
The AUA is a resource for medical students, residents, program directors and residency coordinators. With more than 500 medical students participating in the Urology Residency Match and over 2,000 domestic and international resident members, the AUA promotes the highest standards of urological clinical care through evidence-based urologic education and research, and in the formulation of health care policy.

The AUA administers the SAU Urology Residency Match program for medical students interested in the field of urology. We provide valuable benefits to support our residents during their training, as well as relevant information about fellowships and job opportunities. In addition, we offer grant programs, and provide updated news and information to our program directors and residency coordinators so that they are just as informed as their residents about the AUA.

The Urology Residency Match (Urology Match or SAU Match) is governed by the Society of Academic Urologists. For more than 40 years, the AUA has administered the Urology Residency Match on behalf of the SAU. MetaKeywords: Examination resources, Residency, specialty, Match, residency match, medical students, residents, program directors, Fellowship, residency coordinators
Body:
AUA Self-Assessment Study Program (SASP)

SASP is the AUA's most popular study tool for exam preparation. Developed each year, SASP is a 150-question, multiple-choice practice examination that addresses the core curriculum of medical knowledge and latest advances in patient care. Learn more about the SASP, and how residents can receive exclusive savings at https://cme.auanet.org/Page/SASP.

Annual Review Course

For the ABU Qualifying (Part 1) Examination, residents need to possess basic urologic knowledge and an understanding of current American Urological Association practice guidelines. To fulfill this need, the AUA developed this course to disseminate current urologic knowledge and successfully prepare residents for the ABU examination. This course is also of interest to practicing urologists as well as others, including allied health professionals, looking for a thorough review of basic urologic topics. Learn More

Oral Board Review Course

The purpose of the AUA Oral Board Review Course is to prepare attendees for the American Board of Urology (ABU) Certifying Examination (Part II). The course will provide attendees with valuable practice and practical preparation skills for taking the urology oral board exam. Attendees participate in two-75 minute mock oral exams, an Objective Structured Clinical Examination (OSCE) session, an interactive case analysis with expert examiners, and an “Ask the Experts” panel discussion with Faculty who offer tips & tricks for preparing for and successfully taking the oral examination. Learn More
